hook: "Our best clients are generating their highest performing Meta ads with one format: animated product videos." — client-proof + single-format claim.
cta: "Comment 'ADS' and I'll send the full playbook + workflow." — comment-gated lead magnet.
idea: Animated product videos (any style skin) beat live action on Meta when built on Hook → Problem → Benefit → Solution, producible at 15-20 concepts/day under $100.
sequencing: Hook: best clients' top Meta ads = one format.
The style menu: origami, voxel, Minecraft, Pixar, paper craft.
The constant: same structure — Hook → Problem → Benefit → Solution.
The insight: pair the structure with visuals people want to watch.
The system: drop product in, test run — 15-20 concepts/day under $100.
CTA: comment ADS for the playbook.
33s video thumbnail.
formatting: Text post + 33s animated video (thumbnail only in file). Pitches a style-system: origami, voxel, Minecraft, Pixar, paper craft — same structure, swappable skins.
why_it_works: Separates the variable (style) from the constant (structure) — gives buyers a testable system instead of a one-off. '15-20 concepts a day under $100' makes AI production economics tangible.
what_to_steal: The Hook → Problem → Benefit → Solution skeleton for LC's animated product videos ('Hook: your jewelry turns green → Problem: cheap plating → Benefit: waterproof PVD → Solution: LC'). The style-swap system (same ad, 5 visual skins) is the dupe machine's animation lane.

hook: "🚨 I made a fully animated product video for Amazon without touching a traditional editing workflow." — the 'without' frame promises a shortcut.
cta: Implied: try Dreamina Octo (hashtags #dreamina #dreaminapartner mark it as a sponsored partner post).
idea: Dreamina Octo acts as an AI creative partner that handles storyboarding, motion graphics, animation, and music sync from a single idea — no editing workflow needed.
sequencing: Hook: fully animated product video, no traditional editing.
The tool: Dreamina Octo as AI creative partner.
Capability list: storyboarding → motion graphics → animation → music sync.
The workflow: 'I simply shared the idea, it transformed it.'
6s video demo.
Partner hashtags.
formatting: 6s video (thumbnail only) + punchy text with arrow bullets (→). 190K views — the demo itself is the content; extremely short.
why_it_works: 'Without touching a traditional editing workflow' sells the removal of pain, not the addition of features. The 190K views prove tool-demo content itself is high-interest — the audience wants the shortcut.
what_to_steal: The 'no traditional editing workflow' positioning for LC's internal buy-in: animated product videos don't need an editor anymore. The 4-step pipeline (storyboard → motion → animation → music) is LC's animation production checklist.

hook: "Here's why animated product ads consistently outperform on cold traffic:" — a causal claim ('here's why') aimed at media buyers.
idea: Animation beats live action on cold traffic because curiosity precedes skepticism — a cartoon explaining an ingredient gets watched while a white-coat human gets scrolled past as an obvious ad.
sequencing: Thesis: animated ads outperform on cold traffic.
Mechanism: people are curious before they're skeptical.
Contrast: cartoon character explaining = watched through.
Contrast: white-coat person = scrolled past, registers as ad instantly.
Payoff: animation buys seconds of goodwill that live action loses by looking like a sales pitch.
formatting: Single-paragraph text analysis — no media. Dense, one-idea essay format aimed at advertisers.
why_it_works: Names the exact psychological window (curiosity-before-skepticism) and gives a vivid A/B contrast. 'Buys you a few extra seconds of goodwill' quantifies the mechanism in media-buyer terms.
what_to_steal: The cold-traffic rationale for LC's animated lane: animation earns curiosity-goodwill from unaware audiences who'd scroll a polished jewelry ad. Use this to justify LC's Pixar/claymation product videos as TOF openers.

hook: "Making an animated product ad used to be a project." — past-pain framing; 'used to be' implies the pain is now gone.
cta: "Full tutorial 👇" + link — drives to the how-to.
idea: Animated product ads at scale no longer take a month — the old production bottleneck is dead (tutorial shows how).
sequencing: Pain past-tense: animated ads used to be a project.
Pain past-tense: at scale used to take a month.
Claim: 'We took down both.'
CTA: full tutorial link.
4s video thumbnail.
formatting: Ultra-short text (4 lines) + 4s video thumbnail. Teaser format — the value lives behind the tutorial link.
why_it_works: 'Used to be' is a two-word paradigm shift — it tells the reader the world changed without explaining how, forcing the click. Brevity + curiosity gap.
what_to_steal: The past-tense pain framing for LC's internal/team content ('shooting jewelry content used to take a crew'). The teaser structure works for LC's behind-the-scenes organic posts.

hook: "We're entering an era where your marketing doesn't have to look ordinary." — era-framing makes the reader feel behind.
cta: "🔗 Register:" + link — direct event signup; 'Starts Today, 25th August' adds urgency.
idea: AI Content Lab teaches hologram videos, AI VFX, animated product showcases, and premium promo content — starting today.
sequencing: Era hook: marketing doesn't have to look ordinary.
Promise: with AI, ideas literally come to life.
Offer: join AI Content Lab.
Curriculum: hologram videos, AI VFX, animated showcases, premium promos.
Urgency: starts today, 25th August.
CTA: register link.
13s video thumbnail.
formatting: Promo post + 13s video (thumbnail only). Emoji-formatted event invite: 📅 date line, 🔗 register line.
why_it_works: Era-framing ('we're entering an era') creates FOMO — not buying is being left behind. Naming four concrete deliverables makes the vague 'AI content' promise tangible.
what_to_steal: The format menu as LC's AI-video lane checklist: hologram-style product reveals, AI VFX transitions, animated showcases. 'Your marketing doesn't have to look ordinary' is a usable LC organic hook for its own AI content.

hook: "Hair thinning, 180+ days:" — longevity-as-proof framing; 180+ days running = the ad is a winner.
cta: none in the post itself (research thread; includes a GetHookd MCP prompt for the reader to reuse).
idea: Long-running hair-loss ads reveal the winning patterns: persona pages running AI-animated product videos (The Consumer Pulse, 199 ads, 183 days), Amazon-attribution landers, and UGC/side-by-side tests — with a reusable prompt to replicate the research.
sequencing: Hook: hair thinning ads running 180+ days.
The Consumer Pulse: persona page, 199 ads, AI-animated shampoo bottle, 183 days.
Hair Science: 19s product video → Amazon attribution lander, 301 days.
BodyWise UGC 'don't put this on your face,' 309 days.
Root'd pool side-by-side test vs 'scam fibers,' 215 days.
Vedix USA long-hair UGC talking head + quiz, 190 days.
The reusable GetHookd MCP prompt (5-step research recipe).
Deliverables spec: persona pages, Amazon advertisers, format table, hooks/offers.
formatting: Ad-intelligence research dump: brand-by-brand table (brand | page | format | lander | proof/offer | days active) plus a reusable MCP prompt. Photo attached. Built for media buyers, not consumers.
why_it_works: Days-active is unfakeable proof — it replaces claimed ROAS with observed survival. The reusable prompt turns a research post into a tool, which earns bookmarks from practitioners.
what_to_steal: Two things: (1) the longevity heuristic — LC should sort its own ad library by days-active to find real winners; (2) the AI-animated product video proof point — a 183-day AI-animated shampoo ad validates LC's animated jewelry lane. The persona-page trick (magazine-style page → brand lander) is worth testing for LC advertorials.

product: oraimomate (brand featured in the spec ad)
hook: "Day 1/30 of creating AI-powered ads for brands." — the series frame + day counter creates follow-worthy momentum.
cta: "For the next 30 days, I'll be creating ads for different brands and products." — follow-the-series CTA.
idea: A 3D animated spec ad for @oraimomate demonstrating how AI turns e-commerce products into scroll-stopping content — day 1 of a 30-day brand series.
sequencing: Series hook: Day 1/30 of AI-powered ads for brands.
The specimen: 3D animated product ad for @oraimomate.
The demo claim: AI turns products into scroll-stopping content.
The promise: 30 days, different brands and products.
26s video.
formatting: Portfolio/spec-ad post: 'Day 1/30' series framing + 26s 3D animated product video (thumbnail only). Creator-showcase format.
why_it_works: The day-counter creates a compounding follow incentive — each post promises 29 more. Spec work for real brands doubles as a client-acquisition funnel for the creator.
what_to_steal: The 'Day X/30 making ads for brands' series format is directly stealable for LC's organic: 'Day 1/30 turning jewelry into scroll-stopping AI ads' — it turns production into content. The 3D animated product treatment is LC's hero-product lane.

hook: "Ranking every type of AI ecom ad creative format:" — ranking/tier framing promises a definitive verdict.
idea: AI ecom formats ranked: F = AI avatar reading scripts/street interviews/slideshows; A = talking product ads; S = AI animation, AI singing, AI native statics → advertorial — and all are testable on EcomBos.
sequencing: Hook: ranking every AI ecom format.
F tier: avatar reading script, AI street interviews, slideshow + stock music.
C tier: lifestyle b-roll + VO, meme ads, packshots as cold ads.
B tier: us-vs-them statics, whiteboard explainers, product-in-hand yapper.
A tier: AI before/after, AI podcast clips, talking product ads.
S tier: AI animation, AI singing, AI native statics → advertorial.
CTA: test them all on EcomBos + link.
formatting: Tier-list text post (F/C/B/A/S) ranking AI ecom ad formats, ending in a product plug. Each tier has 3 format examples.
why_it_works: Tier lists turn a product pitch into debatable content — the ranking IS the ad for EcomBos. Placing its own platform as the place to 'test them all' makes the CTA feel like utility, not a pitch.
what_to_steal: The calibration: talking-product ads are A-tier (reliable) while AI animation is S-tier — LC should weight its AI budget toward animation-first. The F-tier warnings are useful guardrails: no script-reading avatars, no slideshow-with-stock-music for LC.
